---
title: "Best Practices"
---

A quick-reference guide to safe, high-quality care when managing external ventricular drains.

## Do's and Don'ts

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| ✔ Confirm EVD setting before interpreting ICP | ✖ Interpret ICP without knowing the drain setting |
| ✔ Check clamp status before transport or procedures | ✖ Keep EVD closed and not monitor ICP |
| ✔ Level the transducer at the tragus | ✖ Clamp EVD and leave the transducer at the level of the heart |
| ✔ Trend ICP and waveform together | ✖ Rely on a single ICP value |
| ✔ Minimize CSF system access | ✖ Access CSF unnecessarily |
| ✔ Use sterile technique for all handling | ✖ Break sterility during manipulation |
| ✔ Secure tubing to prevent dislodgement | ✖ Leave tubing unsecured |
| ✔ Communicate EVD status during handoffs | ✖ Assume others know the EVD setup |
| ✔ Monitor ICP during transport at all times | ✖ Transport without considering ICP risk |
| ✔ Reassess waveform if values seem inconsistent | ✖ Ignore dampened or abnormal waveforms |

## CSF Color Interpretation

| CSF Appearance | Clinical Interpretation |
|---|---|
| **Clear** | Normal CSF |
| **Xanthochromia (yellow)** | Suggests prior hemorrhage or SAH breakdown products |
| **Bloody** | May indicate active bleeding, traumatic tap, or evolving hemorrhage |
| **Cloudy** | Concerning for infection (e.g., ventriculitis) |
| **Debris / Particulate** | Possible clot breakdown, infection, or catheter obstruction |

::: {.callout-warning}
**Clinical Note:** Changes in CSF color should always be interpreted in clinical context and may warrant further evaluation.
:::

## Key Takeaway

::: {.callout-tip}
**Clinical Pearl:** Most EVD-related errors are system-based (leveling, clamping, interpretation). A structured approach prevents harm.
:::
